109	## Non-goals
110	
111	- Bedrock. It drops Claude reasoning signatures and redacted content in the same way
112	  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`). A separate ticket.
113	- A setting for `output_config.effort`, an automatic interleaved-thinking beta header, or a change
114	  to the `ExtendedThinking` options.
115	- A model, API or key check on a block before it goes back. Probe finding 4 shows a cross-model
116	  block is accepted. A block that Anthropic rejects gives the API error unchanged; the README
117	  documents how a host removes the blocks (below).
118	- Exact text order when one response has more than one `text` block. Core joins all text of a
119	  turn into one `Text` part, and the stream records only the first text position. So
120	  `thinking, text A, tool_use, thinking, text B, tool_use` goes back as
121	  `thinking, text AB, tool_use, thinking, tool_use`. Probe finding 4 shows the API does not check
122	  order.
123	- A change to core. Core keeps one `Reasoning` part per message for display. The request translator
124	  does not read it.
125	
126	## Anti-goals
127	
128	- Provider data on responses with no thinking. The SMA-827 rollback note says that an older core
129	  fails on the `provider_data` variant.
130	- A changed request for a history that has no Anthropic provider data.
131	- A failure or warning because of another provider's provider data.
132	- A new failure on a shape that `main` sends today and the API accepts (hand-off transcripts,
133	  resumed sessions, SMA-834 joined rounds, the drop-induced prefill error).
134	
135	## Approaches
136	
137	Sven picked approach A on 2026-11-21.
138	
139	- **A. One provider-data part for each block (picked).** At the stop of each block, the stream
140	  sends one `ProviderData { provider: "anthropic" }`. Thinking blocks carry the whole block. The
141	  first `text` block and each `tool_use` block carry only their position. The request translator
142	  sorts by position. This is the Gemini pattern, it ties each `tool_use` position to its call
143	  through `call_id`, and it agrees with conformance assertion 8.
144	- **B. One part for each response**, sent at `message_stop`, with the ordered block list and
145	  `tool_use` ids as references. Simpler to rebuild, but nothing is kept if the stream stops early,
146	  and the references are not tied to their calls through `call_id`.
147	- **Rejected: thinking first, then text, then `tool_use`.** It loses interleaved order.
148	
149	## Design
150	
151	### Carrier key and data shapes
152	
153	- A new `pub const PROVIDER_DATA_KEY: &str = "anthropic";` in
154	  `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/lib.rs`. It is a wire-format key, separate from
155	  `PROVIDER_ID` (the same string today). Its rustdoc says that a host may filter parts by this key,
156	  but the `data` shape is private to the crate and can change.
157	- The crate reads and writes `data` through one private serde type with a `kind` tag:
158	  - `{"kind":"block","index":n,"block":{"type":"thinking","thinking":"…","signature":"…"}}`, `call_id: None`;
159	  - `{"kind":"block","index":n,"block":{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}}`, `call_id: None`;
160	  - `{"kind":"text","index":n}`, `call_id: None`, for the first text block of the response only;
161	  - `{"kind":"tool_use","index":n}`, `call_id: Some(id)`, where `id` is the `tool_use` id.
162	- `index` is the Anthropic content-block `index` of the response.
163	
164	### Stream (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)
165	
166	- `ContentBlockHead::Thinking` gets `thinking` and `signature` fields with `#[serde(default)]`;
167	  their values start the block state. A new `ContentBlockHead::RedactedThinking { data: String }`
168	  (`"redacted_thinking"`). Remove `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the signature field and on
169	  `ContentBlockStop::index`.
170	- `BlockState::Thinking` keeps the joined text and the signature. `thinking_delta` still emits
171	  `ReasoningDelta`. `signature_delta` appends to the signature. `BlockState::RedactedThinking`
172	  keeps `data`.
173	- On `content_block_stop` for index `n`, the stream removes the block state (a second stop for the
174	  same index only writes a debug log), then:
175	  - thinking with a non-empty signature: emit the `block` part; a thinking block with no signature
176	    is not kept (debug log, index and type only);
177	  - redacted thinking with non-empty data: emit the `block` part;
178	  - the first text block: record a `text` position;
179	  - `tool_use`: record a `tool_use` position, but only for a call that the stream emitted as a
180	    `ToolCallDelta` (`name_emitted`), and never for the synthesized structured-output tool
181	    (`synthesized_tool_index`).
182	- Position records wait until the stream emits the response's first `block` part. Then the stream
183	  emits all waiting records, and after that each new position at its block stop. If the response
184	  emits no `block` part, it emits no position record (Goal 4). Provider-data order has no meaning,
185	  because each part carries its index.
186	- Log lines hold only the index and the block type, never block content.
187	
188	### Core
189	
190	No change. The accumulator stores provider data in arrival order in the turn's `AssistantMessage`,
191	after `Reasoning` and `Text`. Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items sorted by call id. The token
192	estimate counts the `Reasoning` text and the serialized `data` (which holds the text again and the
193	signature). So the estimate is high on models that strip earlier thinking and close on models that
194	keep it in context; this is accepted and documented.
195	
196	### Request translator (`translate/request.rs`)
197	
198	Terms: a **source message** is one `Item::AssistantMessage` together with the `tool_use` blocks
199	that come from it: its own `ContentPart::ToolUse` parts, and the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow
200	it before the next `AssistantMessage` or the next user message with a part that is not a tool
201	result. A `ToolResult` does not end a source message (the SMA-827 Gemini rule).
202	
203	1. **Position map.** For each source message, collect its parts with
204	   `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` that parse as the private type. Ignore other providers' parts with
205	   no log. Skip a part that does not parse, or a `block` that fails the checks below, with a debug
206	   log. A source message with no valid Anthropic part builds exactly as on `main`.
207	2. **Block checks.** Rebuild each block from known fields only: `thinking` needs string `thinking`
208	   (an empty string is valid) and a non-empty string `signature`; `redacted_thinking` needs a
209	   non-empty string `data`. Send only `type` and those fields.
210	3. **Groups.** Each wire assistant message is a list of groups, one group for each source message
211	   that adds blocks to it, in the order the groups are added. Inside a group, each block gets a sort
212	   key:
213	   - a `block` part: its `index`;
214	   - the text block: the `text` position index; with no `text` position, the key is just before
215	     the first `tool_use` block of the group in key order, or after every block when the group has
216	     no `tool_use`;
217	   - a `tool_use` block: the index of the `tool_use` position part with the same `call_id`, taken
218	     and removed in order, so that a repeated id in one source message stays correct; with no
219	     position, it goes after every keyed block, in today's order.
220	   A position part whose `tool_use` is gone (trimmed history) is ignored.
221	4. **Sort.** Sort each group by key (stable), and never compare keys of different groups. Do the
222	   sort in one pass at the end of `translate_messages`, before `apply_cache_strategy`. A `tool_use`
223	   that `close_open_transfers` or another split moves into a different wire message loses its key
224	   and goes after the keyed blocks of its new message.
225	5. **Thinking-only messages.** A wire assistant message that, after all its `tool_use` blocks
226	   join, has no `text` and no `tool_use` block drops its thinking blocks. It then counts as empty,
227	   exactly as on `main` (no flush, not sent, the drop-induced prefill flag unchanged). The decision
228	   looks ahead over the items, because the `tool_use` blocks come from later items. This keeps
229	   hand-off transcripts (`thread_handoff_transcript` removes tool calls and keeps assistant
230	   messages), `Length` finishes after a thinking block, and
231	   `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` as on `main`.
232	6. **SMA-834 join rule.** An assistant message joins an open round when every block is
233	   `tool_use`, `thinking` or `redacted_thinking`, the pending results are not empty, and the round
234	   is open. This covers the nested form (`[ProviderData thinking, ToolUse]`) and the form that the
235	   accumulator writes (`AssistantMessage[Reasoning, ProviderData]` then `Item::ToolCall`).
236	7. **Reasoning.** `ContentPart::Reasoning` is never sent. Its drop logs at debug level, not warn.
237	8. **Cache.** `apply_cache_strategy` never puts `cache_control` on a `thinking` or
238	   `redacted_thinking` block. If the last block is one of them, it uses the last other block of
239	   that message, or no breakpoint.
240	9. **Which turns.** Every assistant message in the history (see "Which turns send blocks back"). The `thinking` setting of the request is not
241	   changed by the history.

```rust
use paigasus_helikon::anthropic::AnthropicModel;

let model = AnthropicModel::messages("claude-sonnet-4-6").build()?;
```

`AnthropicModel::messages(id)` returns an `AnthropicModelBuilder`; `build()`
yields a `Result<AnthropicModel, BuildError>`.

Anthropic uses provider tool types. If a tool declares an `anthropic` type, the adapter sends the typed entry, for example `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`, with no description and no input schema. To turn this off, call `native_tool_types(false)` on the builder. The adapter then sends the generic schema. See [Provider tool types](./tools.md#provider-tool-types).

Anthropic thinking blocks round trip through provider data. The stream keeps each `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` block as a `ContentPart::ProviderData` part with the key `PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` (`"anthropic"`). The next request sends the eligible blocks back unchanged, and only with `Adaptive` or `Enabled`. The shape of the `data` is private.

- The beta `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` has an effect only on models with manual interleaving, with `ExtendedThinking::Enabled`. These models are Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and earlier Claude 4 models. Add `.beta("interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14")` to let the model think again after a tool result. Claude Haiku 4.5 ignores the beta. `Adaptive` interleaves by itself.
- With `ExtendedThinking::Disabled` (the default), the provider sends no thinking block back. On a model that thinks by default, for example `claude-sonnet-5-5`, set `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive` to keep the reasoning between tool calls. The provider then also sends `drop_block`.
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` needs `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`.
- With `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`, the provider sends `block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior = "drop_block"` and the beta header `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`. If the history before a thinking block changed, the API drops that block and every later thinking block. The model loses that reasoning. The request does not fail. Examples are a hand-off with other `system` text or tools, and an edit of an earlier message.
- With `ExtendedThinking::Enabled`, the provider sends no binding. Use `Enabled` only on models that do not run the prefix check, for example `claude-haiku-4-5`. Claude Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5 and Fable reject `Enabled`.
- The default sends no effort, and the model uses its own default. On some models, for example `claude-sonnet-5-5` with the default `medium`, adaptive thinking can skip thinking on a short task. A higher effort makes thinking more likely. In a test, `claude-sonnet-5-5` skipped thinking on a short tool task at `medium` and at `high`, and it thought at `max`. To set the effort, call `.effort(Effort::Max)` on the builder. The provider then sends `output_config: { effort: "max" }`. Some models reject this field, so set it only for a model that supports effort.
- Measured on Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.5 with `Enabled { budget_tokens: 2048 }`, each round sent about 100 more input tokens without the beta header, and about 250 to 300 with it.
- If Anthropic rejects one block, each later request of the session fails. To recover, remove every part with `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` from the stored history.
- The thinking text is stored two times. A host that removes `Reasoning` must also remove these parts. If a host removes these parts, the SDK cannot send the thinking blocks back.

### Bedrock — `paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`

Reached as `paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel` behind the `bedrock`
feature. Covers the **Converse streaming API** — tool use and multi-turn

## Extended thinking in a tool loop

The stream keeps each `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` block as a `ContentPart::ProviderData` part with the key `PROVIDER_DATA_KEY`. The next request sends the eligible blocks back unchanged. The rules below say which blocks are eligible, and only `Adaptive` and `Enabled` send them. The shape of the `data` is private to this crate.

A thinking block is sent back only in the same assistant message as a text block or a `tool_use` block of its own response. If its response had `tool_use` blocks, one of them must be in that message. So after a hand-off that removed the tool calls of a response, or when the history lost those calls, the SDK sends no thinking block of that response. At the end of a history, the SDK sends no thinking block in a last assistant message. With `ExtendedThinking::Disabled`, the SDK sends no thinking block at all. The cache never marks a thinking block as a breakpoint. A response with no kept thinking block writes no provider data.

- The beta `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` has an effect only on models with manual interleaving, with `ExtendedThinking::Enabled`. These models are Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and earlier Claude 4 models. Add `.beta("interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14")` to the builder. Then the model can think again after a tool result. Claude Haiku 4.5 ignores the beta. `Adaptive` interleaves by itself.

- `claude-sonnet-5-5` needs `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`.
- With `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`, the provider sends `block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior = "drop_block"` and the beta header `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`. If the history before a thinking block changed, the API drops that block and every later thinking block. The model loses that reasoning. The request does not fail. Examples are a hand-off with other `system` text or tools, and an edit of an earlier message.

Some models reject this field, so set it only for a model that supports effort.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The core idea is sound. A per-block byte length with a sum check validates itself, stays in one crate, and falls back to today's bytes for old data and for most unknown shapes. Three gaps must close first: (1) the split survives the paths that drop the thinking blocks, which breaks the SMA-840 "builds as if it had no Anthropic part" contract on hand-off transcripts; (2) the cut order is ambiguous, and one reading can silently reorder text; (3) the fallback tests cannot fail against the current code.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None

### MAJOR
- **The split survives the drop paths, so the SMA-840 contract breaks** - The spec splits in `assistant_blocks`. Two later passes then drop the thinking but keep the pieces as separate text blocks:
  - `drop_thinking_without_own_block` clears the slots of a lost group (`translate/request.rs:552-566`).
  - `into_output` removes the thinking from the last assistant message and clears the slots (`request.rs:527-532`).
  The documented contract says "When a rule fails, the thinking blocks are dropped, and the item builds as if it had no Anthropic part" (`request.rs:225-228`). The SMA-840 tests check exactly this with `without_anthropic` equality (`request.rs:2769-2772`, `2794`, `2817`, `2976`). With `len` data, `without_anthropic` gives one `text "AB"` block, but the new code gives `text "A"`, `text "B"`. | Why it matters: hand-off is a common path. `thread_handoff_transcript` (`paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:770-789`) removes the `ToolCall` items and keeps the `AssistantMessage` parts. Every multi-text response with tool calls then reaches the lost-group path. The API accepts adjacent text blocks, so nothing fails. But the invariant breaks silently, because every existing test uses `text_pos` with no `len` and takes the fallback. | Suggested fix: build one text `WireBlock` that carries its split plan (piece keys and byte ranges), with the key of the first position. Expand it in `WireMessage::into_value` after `drop_thinking_without_own_block`, and only while the block still has a slot. The last message and lost groups then keep one joined block, as today. The keep rule does not change, because a concatenation is blank only when every piece is blank. Add replay tests with `len` data for a hand-off transcript, for lost calls, and for a last assistant message. Each test asserts `messages(&items) == messages(&without_anthropic(&items))`.
- **The cut order is ambiguous, and one reading reorders text** - The replay rules say "Collect all `Text` positions of the message in part order", and then "cut the text into one piece per position, in position order". Stream data gives the same order both ways, because blocks stop in index order and the `waiting_positions` flush keeps queue order (`stream.rs:314-317`). Hand-built or reordered parts can differ. Take positions `[(3,len 1),(1,len 1)]` in part order and the text `"AB"`. A part-order cut gives `"A"`→`At(3,1)` and `"B"`→`At(1,1)`. `sort_groups` (`request.rs:597-601`) then sends `"B"`, `"A"`. | Why it matters: the model silently gets the history text in the wrong order. No check catches this, because the sum still matches. | Suggested fix: add a splittable condition. The `Text` indexes in part order must be strictly increasing, with no duplicates. If not, fall back. Then state "cut in part order". Also fall back when a `Text` index is the same as a `Block` or `ToolUse` index of the message, because equal keys sort in no defined order.
- **The test plan cannot prove that the fallback guards work, and it misses the risky shapes** - The three fallback tests (a length mismatch, a missing `len`, a cut that is not on a char boundary) pass on the current code without any change. They do not show that the guard, and not some other cause, stops the split. Also not covered:
  - The drop paths above.
  - The stream shapes that make the sum fall short: a text block whose stop never arrives, a `text_delta` for an index that is not open (`stream.rs:142-144` emits `TokenDelta` for any index), a block stop after the terminal event (`stream.rs:243-250`), and a repeated `content_block_start` that resets the counter.
  - Text before the first kept thinking block, end to end: `[Text A(0), Thinking(1), Text B(2), ToolUse(3)]` must replay as `[A, Th1, B, tu3]`.
  - An empty first text block, `[Th0, Text ""(1), tu2, Th3, Text "B"(4), tu5]`. Today "B" goes to index 1. The new code puts it at index 4. This is a real fix, and the test is red on today's code.
  - A positive multi-byte split, for example `"é"` and `"ü"`.
  - The "more than one text part" fallback. The spec lists this case but has no test for it.
  - The multi-text shape in `session_projection_round_trip` (`translate/mod.rs:1337`).
  Also, the existing test `two_text_blocks_join_at_first_text_position` (`translate/mod.rs:1277-1313`) asserts `"AB"` and will fail. The spec says only that the "single-text tests get the `len` field". | Why it matters: the user's memory records that reviews passed code that had regressions, because the tests checked against a spec, not against the baseline. Characterization-only fallback tests repeat that pattern. | Suggested fix: pair each fallback test with a control that uses the same data with correct `len` values and does split. Add the shapes listed above. Rename and invert the `two_text_blocks_join...` test. A structured-output test needs hand-built events, because the API rejects a forced `tool_choice` with thinking on (`live_round_trip.rs:126`, `response_format.rs:67,76`).

### MINOR
- **"A host edited the text" does not always fall back** - An edit that keeps the byte length (for example a redaction from "John" to "XXXX") passes the sum check and splits. This is harmless, because the pieces are contiguous slices, so their concatenation is always the edited text. The other side: an edit that changes the length falls back even when it is after the last thinking block, which the SMA-840 probe says the API accepts (`2026-11-21-sma-840-...-design.md:356`). | Why it matters: the spec states the behaviour incorrectly. | Suggested fix: correct the "Cases that fall back" list. Say that an equal-length edit splits and that this is harmless.
- **A dropped blank piece changes the replayed bytes and leaves one shape unfixed** - In `[Th0, Text "\n\n"(1), Th2, Text "B"(3)]` the blank piece is dropped, so `Th2` still has a changed prefix. Today's joined replay sends the `"\n\n"`. The split replay does not. This is not a regression: I found no shape where today keeps a thinking block that the split loses. | Suggested fix: write this down as a known limit, so the decision is on record.
- **Stored `len` values are untrusted, and the spec does not forbid a panic** - The spec checks only char boundaries. A stored `len` of `u64::MAX` overflows the sum: a debug build panics, and a release build wraps. A wrapped sum can pass the check and then slice out of range. `from_part` already treats this data as untrusted (`provider_data.rs:126-133`). | Why it matters: a panic in `build_body` fails every later request of that session. | Suggested fix: require `checked_add`, `usize::try_from`, and `str::get` with no panic, and fall back on any failure. Add a test with `len: u64::MAX`.
- **No log on fallback** - A fallback is silent, so the debugger cannot tell why a response lost `Thinking(2)`. | Suggested fix: add a `tracing::debug!` with the reason (no `len`, sum mismatch, boundary, order) and the lengths only, never the content, as the crate already does (`provider_data.rs:110-113`). Also log a `text_delta` for an index that is not an open text block, in the style of `stream.rs:158-162`.
- **The rollback and release facts are not stated** - The old code reads new data safely. `AnthropicData` has no `deny_unknown_fields` (`provider_data.rs:75-77`), and `text_seen` takes the first position (`request.rs:702`). But after a downgrade, a later thinking block whose signature includes the split prefix gets dropped one time under `drop_block`. SMA-840 has not shipped yet: the CHANGELOG lists it nowhere, and 0.3.1 holds only a core update (`CHANGELOG.md:8-14`). So "old data without `len`" exists only for users who build from `main`. | Suggested fix: add a short rollout note. Keep `Option<u64>`, because it costs little. Now, before the first release writes this shape into stored sessions, is the cheapest time to set the field name. Consider `bytes`, or document `len` as "UTF-8 bytes".
- **In-code docs that the spec does not list** - These say "first text block": the module doc at `request.rs:7-12`, the comments at `request.rs:701` and `729-730`, and the `AnthropicData::Text` doc at `provider_data.rs:85`. The spec's book reference is `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md`, not `model-providers.md`. Separately, the core `ModelTurn` doc (`core/src/model.rs:573-575`) says "text, reasoning and/or provider data, in that order", but `build_items` puts `Reasoning` first (`model.rs:627-633`). The spec repeats this incorrect order. The design does not depend on the order, so this is only a doc fix.

### QUESTIONS
- Did a live probe show that today's joined replay drops `Thinking(2)`, and that the split replay keeps it? The SMA-840 table covers "inserted a text block before the thinking block", not "text joined across a thinking block". The SMA-840 non-goal (`...sma-840...-design.md:121-122`) also says "Probe finding 4 shows the API does not check order", which disagrees with this spec. The API returns `input_transformations` when it drops a block (`...sma-840...-design.md:343`), so a probe or an ignored live test can observe the result.
- Should the last assistant message (prefill or continuation) send one joined text block, as today? The first MAJOR finding recommends yes.
- Is there a captured trace of a multi-text response with interleaved thinking, for a fixture with a provenance header (CONTRIBUTING, "Wire-format fixtures")? Hand-built event lists are acceptable for unit tests.
- Text blocks with citations: the parser skips `citations_delta` (an unknown variant makes the event fail to parse, and the event is skipped), so the replay sends the text with no citations. That probably still changes the prefix. Is this a known limit to record?

## What's good
- The sum check validates itself. Each source of extra `TokenDelta` bytes makes the sum fall short, so the translator falls back to today's bytes with no special code. Examples are synthesized JSON (`stream.rs:166-168`), deltas for an index that is not open, missing stops, stops after the terminal event, and backends that normalize text. Old data falls back, and old code ignores `len`.
- I checked these invariants, and they hold. A text block is present after the split exactly when it was present before (a concatenation is blank only when every piece is blank). So `only_tool_uses`, `thinking_only`, `joins`, the tentative and rollback path (only for thinking-only items, which have no text), `is_kept_by`, and the `BeforeFirstToolUse` resolution all decide the same as today. The `Disabled` path is unchanged, because `strip_own_provider_data` removes the positions first (`translate/mod.rs:18-36`). The API does not reject adjacent text blocks, and the split never makes "the message starts with text" more likely.
- The scope is tight. There is no core change, the rejected alternatives have good reasons, and the cut logic is a pure function that is easy to unit test.
